claims.exact_statement: For every m>=1 and every nonzero signed two-point function on F_2^m, its normalized squared Walsh law is product if and only if the two support points differ in exactly one coordinate. In that case the law is uniform on s_i=b, has entropy m-1, and mean degree (m-1)/2+b, where b=0 for equal signs and b=1 for opposite signs.
hypotheses: exactly two nonzero values, each in {-1,1}
proof_dependencies: support of a product law is a coordinate subcube
claims.refutes: The proposed enlargement by non-coordinate affine pairs under the retained product-row hypothesis.

claims.exact_statement: In the two-address, four-physical-bit family with three pairwise-disjoint signed two-point conditional cells and a product normalized squared law in every conditional row, H/I<=40/17. Equality is attained by the archived constant-sign witness. Each alternating edge sign preserves H and adds exactly 1/8 to I.
hypotheses: two address bits and four physical bits
three pairwise-disjoint signed two-point conditional cells
residual sign pattern on the complement
all normalized conditional squared Walsh laws are product
uniform cube, Shannon entropy in bits
claims.refutes: Existence of a ratio above 40/17 in the frozen signed two-point product-cell family.
claims.first_unproved_line: C022 remains open for higher-support conditional product rows and arbitrary physical dimension.
